title: Pasta with Cream Sauce and Added Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with cream sauce and added vegetables is a home recipe (3620) that combines cooked pasta, a smooth cream sauce, and a variety of fresh vegetables such as broccoli, carrots, bell pepper, and zucchini. The dish is flavorful, quick to prepare, and suitable for lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cream sauce is often made from heavy cream, butter, and Parmesan, giving the dish a velvety texture.
Vegetables retain most of their vitamins when lightly sautéed or blanched before being mixed into the pasta.
Cooking pasta "al dente" helps it hold onto the sauce better, creating a more harmonious bite.
A homemade recipe allows you to control salt and fat levels, making it healthier than many store‑bought sauces.
Traditional Italian cuisine often uses fettuccine or penne for creamy sauces like this.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Durum wheat pasta provides B1, B2, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables such as broccoli and carrots add fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: The cream sauce with Parmesan and vegetables supplies antioxidants (vitamin E, carotenoids) that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Cheese and cream are sources of calcium and phosphorus, essential for strong bones.

items.title: Balanced protein‑carbohydrate combo
items.content: Pasta provides complex carbs while the sauce and vegetables contribute plant‑based and dairy proteins.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Cream sauce can be calorie‑dense and contain saturated fat; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cream and cheese may cause discomfort for those with lactose intolerance; plant‑based alternatives can be used.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to dairy should avoid the traditional sauce or substitute with non‑dairy options.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Parmesan adds salt; reduce added salt if you need to limit sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, garnished with fresh herbs (parsley, basil) and extra grated Parmesan if desired. It pairs well with a light side salad or whole‑grain bread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of milk or cream to restore the sauce's creaminess.
